answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a trust graph where multi-agent auditing evaluates topological cut verifications. When synthetic identities attempt to bridge fake communities across a sparse graph cut, verifiers detect the choke point and trigger stake slashing. Like channeling turbulent flow along a secure river, this network creates a superlinear attacker cost: forging cut-edge consensus requires exponential capital that dissolves unless backed by authentic, jade collateral.
